notes.text: Wisdom — It is a great question what this wisdom is. Some understand it of the Divine wisdom; others of the second person in the Godhead: and it cannot be denied that some passages best agree to the former, and others to the latter opinion. Possibly both may be joined together, and the chapter may be understood of Christ considered partly in his personal capacity, and partly in regard of his office, which was to impart the mind and will of God to mankind.
High place — Where she may be best seen and heard. Paths - Where many paths meet, where there is a great concourse, and where travelers may need direction.
Gates — The places of judgment, and of the confluence of people. The entry - To invite passengers at their first coming and to conduct them to her house. The doors - Of her house.
O men — To all men without exception.

glossa.text: *Doth not wisdom,* etc. The Lord has spoken openly to the world: and in secret he has spoken nothing. Why then, his Gospel being neglected, do wretched men flow together to heresy and to wantonness?
*In the highest places,* etc. On the mountain he taught the disciples and the crowds together, etc, *as far as* who speak against him in secret?
*O ye men, to you.* He cries out to men, that is, to strenuous hearers of the word: for in either sex the women, that is, the loose minds, cannot receive the words of wisdom.

notes.text: In — Not only in Israel, but among all nations. Which shews that this psalm speaks of the Messiah, and the times of the New Testament. Heavens - Where thy throne of glory is established, where the blessed angels celebrate thy praises, where Christ sitteth at thy right hand in glorious majesty, from whence he poureth down excellent gifts upon babes.

Babes — Weak and foolish, and contemptible persons, who are frequently called babes or children. Such are very unfit to grapple with an enemy: and therefore when such persons conquer the most powerful and malicious enemies, it must needs confound them, and advance the glory of God: as indeed it did, when such mean persons as the apostles, and disciples of Christ, maintained and propagated the gospel, in spite of all the wit, power, and rage of their enemies. Ordained - Perfectly or firmly settled strength; that is, the praise of his strength or power, Matt. xxi, 16, it is rendered praise. Still - Silence and confound them. Avenger - The devil, and all who are his vassals and espouse his quarrel.

The moon — Either the sun is included under this general title: or he omitted it, because he made this psalm by night. Ordained - Placed in that excellent and unalterable order, and directed to their several motions.

What is man — How mean and inconsiderable a thing is man, if compared with thy glorious majesty. Man - Hebrew. infirm, or miserable man. By which it is apparent that he speaks of man, not according to the state of his creation, but as fallen into a state of sin and misery, and mortality. Mindful - Carest for him, and conferest such high favours upon him. The son - Hebrew. the son of Adam, that great apostate from God, the sinful son of a sinful father, his son by likeness of disposition and manners, no less than by procreation. All which tends to magnify the following mercy. Visitest - Not in anger, as that word is sometimes used, but with thy grace and mercy.

For — Thou hast in Christ mercifully restored man to his primitive estate, wherein he was but one remove below the angels; from which he was fallen by sin. Crowned - Man, fallen and lost man: who is actually restored to glory and dominion in Christ his head and representative, who received this crown and dominion for man's good, and in his stead; which he will in due time communicate to his members. And so the two expositions of this place concerning mankind and concerning Christ, may be reconciled. For he speaks of that honourable estate conferred first upon Christ, and then by his hands upon mankind. But the words more literally rendered are, Thou madest him a little less than God. And hence some have inferred, that man in his original state was the highest of all creatures. David praises God for giving him victory over his enemies, ver. 1-6. Triumphs in confidence that God would judge the world and protect his people, ver. 7-10. Calls others to praise him, ver. 11, 12. Prays for help, and praises God, ver. 13-20. To the chief musician upon Muth-labben, A psalm of David Title of the psalm. Muth-labben - This also seems to be a title of some tune, or instrument: of which we may be content to be ignorant, as the Jewish doctors are.

glossa.text: « O Lord, our Lord, how admirable is thy name! etc. » ((CASS.)) First the praises of God, his majesty, and his exalted working are described. « In the whole. » ((Ibid.)) Let not the Jews therefore, or any others, claim for themselves what belongs to all, which is the intent. « Above the heavens. » ((AUG.)) Literally, or the Scriptures: because it exceeds the utterances of all the Scriptures; or, « above the heavens. » Continuing with what follows, that is, into the Scriptures, which he bends down to babes, on account of the enemies of the cross: who are destroyed, when the Scriptures are seen, that is, understood, to be led down as far as babes: and when through them they are nourished unto strength, and are raised to the sublimity of understanding.

« Out of the mouth of infants. » ((Ibid.)) Of the unwise, to whom the Apostle gave milk, whom those signified who praised the Lord, in whom the Lord uses this testimony. Out of these he hath perfected praise, because if only the perfect were in the Church, no counsel would be taken for the human race; as now, when even the least, not yet capable of the knowledge of spiritual things, are nourished by faith in the history of things temporal. « Enemies » are all who speak things contrary to the dispensation made through the Crucified. « Defenders » the heretics seem of the faith, the philosophers of wisdom, although yet the former impugn the faith, and the latter true wisdom. « Sucklings, » ((CASS.)) not in age, but as Peter has it, « as newborn babes ((I Petr. II)), » who cannot yet take food, but milk; and it is: thou art proclaimed not only by the perfect, but also by the unwise. Or, he calls infants and sucklings the apostles, who were simple and unlearned men; whence: « The foolish things of the world « God hath chosen, that he may confound the strong ((I Cor. I)). » The praise is more perfect. Or, out of the mouth of infants and sucklings, that is, out of the words of the Hebrew children thou hast perfected praise, which seemed to be done childishly, on account of the enemies, that it might not seem to be human wisdom, but divinely given. « Thine enemies. » The pagans. « The enemy. » The Jew, who is an enemy of God, while he defends the Father alone: because « he that honoureth not the Son, honoureth not « the Father, » or an enemy in his will.

« For I shall see. » Before the Jew, in spirit. « Thy heavens, » the apostles, I shall see present in their descendants; this well suits those of the first age. « The works of thy fingers. » Because they are perfected by the cooperation of the Trinity, which is signified here in the three fingers, as there: « Who weigheth the bulk of the earth with three fingers. » ((Isa. XL.)) And through them, « The moon and the stars which thou hast founded. » Not they.

« What is man. » ((Ibid.)) Secondly, he says that the nature of man, once corrupted, is exalted in Christ above all things. For before he had shown the omnipotence of the Godhead. By man, sinners; by the son of man, the spiritual. ((Ibid.)) Man, any vile person, of whom God is mindful in showing mercy, the Son of man, Christ as man: since through him thou visitest him, when the Word was made flesh, in which the physician came to the sick. « Or the son. » ((AUG.)) The disjunction hints that there is a distance between man and the son of man. Every son of man is man, but not conversely, as Adam. Every man therefore, who bears the image of the earthly: the Son of man, who is heavenly, and deservedly a new man, son of man: because the new is made out of the old by a certain change. ((AUG.)) Why, leaving the higher things, does he speak of these lowest ones? But the sheep, etc., *as far as* who by the seed of the word of God make the hearts of men to bear fruit.

« Moreover the cattle also. » He notes therefore that the wicked also are subject to Christ, which seems less: for these carnal men dwell in the breadth of the plain, that is, in the amplitude of pleasures, not in the mountains of virtues. « The cattle of the field. » ((Ibid.)) Who live in the flesh, where they climb nothing steep: but the broad way, to which they cling, is that which leads to destruction: whence also Abel is slain in the field.

« The birds, » the proud: of whom, « They have set their mouth against heaven ((Psal. LXXII)). » Whose head says: « I will ascend into heaven, and I will exalt my throne, and I will be like the Most High ((Isa. XIV)). « The fishes of the sea that walk through the paths of the sea, » the curious. These three, the pleasure of the flesh, pride, curiosity, include all vices, which are the concupiscence of the flesh, the ambition of the world, that is, pride, the concupiscence of the eyes, since through the eyes curiosity chiefly prevails.

notes.text: Being justified by faith — This is the sum of the preceding chapters. We have peace with God - Being enemies to God no longer, ver. 10; neither fearing his wrath, ver. 9. We have peace, hope, love, and power over sin, the sum of the fifth, sixth, seventh, and eighth chapters. These are the fruits of justifying faith: where these are not, that faith is not.
Into this grace — This state of favour.

We glory in tribulations also — Which we are so far from esteeming a mark of God's displeasure, that we receive them as tokens of his fatherly love, whereby we are prepared for a more exalted happiness. The Jews objected to the persecuted state of the Christians as inconsistent with the people of the Messiah. It is therefore with great propriety that the apostle so often mentions the blessings arising from this very thing.
And patience works more experience of the sincerity of our grace, and of God's power and faithfulness.

Hope shameth us not — That is, gives us the highest glorying. We glory in this our hope, because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts - The divine conviction of God's love to us, and that love to God which is both the earnest and the beginning of heaven. By the Holy Ghost - The efficient cause of all these present blessings, and the earnest of those to come.

glossa.text: *From faith.* Above he said, justified freely by grace, lest faith itself be proud. Let not the faithful man say: that I may merit justification, I have faith: for it is answered him: what hast thou that thou hast not received? *Let us have peace,* we who have been reconciled to him through Christ, the minister of grace.
*Through whom.* He enumerates the benefits that are had from Christ.

*Tribulation.* That tribulation does not take away patience, charity brings about, which is the proper gift of the Holy Spirit.

*Hope.* That is, the certitude of future glory, which to human reason seems empty: but it is confirmed by the testimony of virtue, that is, of patience or of miracles.

*But hope.* Because it is in God, who does not deceive, not in lying man; and the pledge of this hope is the Spirit: for it is read: *Let the fountain of thy water be thine own, and let no stranger have communication with thee ((Eccli. V))*; he himself is the Spirit, whom the wicked cannot receive, and he is charity, which no one can have and be wicked. But a man can have the name of Christ and baptism, receive the body of the Lord, and have the other sacraments, and be wicked. Charity therefore is the proper gift of the Spirit, and the singular fountain.

*The charity of God.* Or: God loves us widely: and we have this in our hearts through the Spirit, who makes us understand the charity of God toward us.

notes.text: I have yet many things to say — Concerning my passion, death, resurrection, and the consequences of it. These things we have, not in uncertain traditions, but in the Acts, the Epistles, and the Revelation. But ye cannot bear them now - Both because of your littleness of faith, and your immoderate sorrow.

When he is come — It is universally allowed that the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost dwell in all believers. And the internal agency of the Holy Ghost is generally admitted. That of the Father and the Son, as represented in this Gospel, deserves our deepest consideration.
All things that the Father hath are mine — Could any creature say this?

glossa.text:
*All truth,* etc. He promises what the Spirit is to do wholly, not that in this life the whole be accomplished.

*Of himself,* etc. ((AUG.)) Because he is not of himself, because the Father alone, etc., *as far as* he always knew, knows and will know.

*He shall glorify me.* Because by making you spiritual he will declare how the Son is equal to the Father, whom according to the flesh, as a man, they had known; or, by taking away fear, he will make you announce my glory to the whole world, which glory profits not me, but men.

*Of mine.* Not that the Spirit is less than the Son. But why he said this, he explains: *All things whatsoever the Father hath are mine.* Therefore I said that he shall receive of mine. Therefore the Spirit receives from the Father, whence the Son receives, because in this Trinity the Son is born of the Father, the Spirit proceeds from the Father. But he who is born of none and proceeds from none is the Father alone.
*All things,* etc. ((AUG.)) Christ speaks concerning the Spirit. *The Spirit of the Father,* etc., *as far as* so openly is it shown that the Spirit is of the Father and of the Son.

registers.label: Spare
lines: When we look up at the heavens, the work of your fingers,
what are we, that you keep us in mind?
Yet you crowned us with glory, and Wisdom danced at your side before the world began.
You set the stars, and still you call us your own.
The Spirit leads us into all the truth, the love of God poured into our hearts.
Father, Son, and Spirit, we lift our praise.
Come, let us worship the God whose name fills the earth.
How majestic is your name in all the earth! Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Step outside on a clear night and tilt your head back — the moon and the stars you set in their places, more than you could ever count.
How majestic is your name in all the earth!
And the wonder is this: the God who flung those stars knows your name, keeps you in mind, crowns you with glory and honor.
How majestic is your name in all the earth!
Before the mountains, before the seas, Wisdom was there, rejoicing, delighting in the human family God would make.
How majestic is your name in all the earth!
Now the Spirit guides us into truth, and the love of God is poured into our hearts like rain on dry ground. Come, lift your eyes and worship.
How majestic is your name in all the earth! Glory to God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Lift your eyes to the stars God set in place.
How majestic is your name!
The Maker of all that light still keeps us in mind.
How majestic is your name!
Wisdom delighted here; the Spirit leads us on.
How majestic is your name!
Come, worship Father, Son, and Spirit.
How majestic is your name in all the earth! Amen.
